assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing turned a single-molecule/surface chemistry idea (reversible terminators, clonal clusters on a flow cell, and in parallel pyrosequencing in picoliter wells) into a quantitative measurement platform that cut the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude. The principle is clear, the capability is genuinely new, and it opened genomics, diagnostics and evolutionary biology; this is the kind of prize I can explain to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: The decisive chemistry-driven contributions appear to be the Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis approach of Balasubramanian and Klenerman and the 454 pyrosequencing-in-picoliter-wells platform led by Rothberg. Ju, Mayer and others contributed reversible-terminator and cluster concepts, so a three-person cut leaves out credible contributors.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of dominant, independently confirmed use; recognition is clearly timely or overdue. Later long-read and other platforms do not undermine the original discovery.
uncertainties: Exactly how credit divides among Solexa, 454 and the reversible-terminator and cluster-amplification contributors is not something I can settle from the supplied text.
Committee may judge this more biology/technology than chemistry, though the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry is central.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible, with ligand design controlling a mechanistically well-understood catalytic cycle. It is ubiquitous in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis and is a textbook example of mechanism-guided catalyst development enabling new capability.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-controlled methods and mechanistic understanding independently; Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor, which complicates but does not prevent a two-person citation.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent confirmation and industrial use. The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make the committee hesitant about overlap, but C-N coupling is a distinct bond-forming capability.
uncertainties: Possible reluctance because of the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Treatment of Kosugi's priority and the fair weighting of the ligand-development contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one DNA base to another without double-strand cleavage, using an engineered deaminase fused to a programmable DNA-binding protein. This is a clear new chemical capability on genomic DNA with immediate therapeutic reach, fitting my interest in discoveries that open vast possibilities. It follows the CRISPR prize of 2020 but is a distinct, chemically conceived invention.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory conceived and developed the approach, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related deaminase-based approach. A Liu-alone citation is cleanest, while group allocation is open to debate.
assessment.maturity: Roughly ten years old, with first clinical results and many independent uses; early but strengthening. Long-term therapeutic outcomes are not yet established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as premature relative to long-term clinical safety data.
Credit for Nishida/Kondo versus Liu's group and the trainees.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single molecules of DNA by the ionic current they produce while threading a nanopore is, to me, an especially elegant union of physics, chemistry and engineering: a clear measurement principle, a protein engineering component, and a new analytical capability including long reads and direct RNA/modified-base detection. It plays well to my interest in single-molecule nanoscale devices.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer showed that polynucleotides can be detected translocating a pore; Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson demonstrated controlled, enzyme-ratcheted base discrimination. Branton may have died (my recollection, unverified), which would affect the available configuration.
assessment.maturity: Commercial nanopore sequencing is established and independently confirmed, though the technology continues to evolve; timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Branton's current status and the supplied credit list leave the best three-person configuration unclear.
Whether the discovery is judged to sit in chemistry rather than physics/biotechnology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a spectacular rise in solar-cell efficiency in a few years, tied to favourable physics (strong absorption, long carrier diffusion lengths, defect tolerance). The generative potential for optoelectronics is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers; Park's group made the solid-state cell; Snaith drove the planar/meso-superstructured high-efficiency devices; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have strong claims. A three-person limit makes the configuration contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency confirmed independently and widely, but long-term stability and toxicity are unresolved; the field is still moving and may be early.
uncertainties: Real dispute about credit among at least six names.
Stability and commercial viability not yet demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method unified electronic structure and molecular dynamics with a fictitious-dynamics Lagrangian, giving ab initio dynamics of condensed-phase and reacting systems. It is a clean physical idea of fundamental importance to simulation of water, solids and reactions.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has exactly two authors, so the credited configuration is clean and unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and independent validation; clearly mature, and arguably the long wait is itself an argument for timeliness. Theory/computation recognition recently came for 2013 (multiscale) and 1998 (DFT).
uncertainties: Possible committee view that the area is partly covered by earlier computational prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reverses the usual inhibitor logic by chemically recruiting an E3 ligase to destroy a target; PROTACs and glue degraders open previously undruggable targets. The concept is new and has generated a large field of chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived PROTACs and Crews drove the field; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, underlying molecular glues. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others also made significant contributions, so the credit is spread.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are advancing but no approvals of PROTAC drugs are established; recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue strands may require a compound citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells brings a physical-chemistry concept (condensation, phase boundaries, multivalent interactions) to cell biology, a perspective I find compelling and widely applicable.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen provided multivalent-interaction phase-separation models. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar understanding, so the credit is broad.
assessment.maturity: The central observations are well replicated, but the physiological significance and interpretation of many condensates remain debated, so the field may not be settled.
uncertainties: Ongoing controversy over in vivo relevance and mechanism.
Whether the contribution is chemistry rather than biology for a citation.
